name: Earthquake
behaviourNotes: Taiwan's whole bag series is built around this scenario: keep the bag by the door so it can be grabbed immediately if a building is damaged and evacuation is required. [TW]
Put on sturdy shoes before moving around afterward - broken glass on the floor is a common injury source. [SG]
If trapped under debris, use a whistle, a torchlight, or tap on a pipe or wall to attract rescuers' attention. [SG]
Keep calm and douse any open flames immediately; take cover under sturdy furniture, away from glass. [HK]
After the shaking stops, check for a gas leak before using any flame - open windows, shut off the main valve, and report it. [HK]

name: Flood
tagline: Rising water from storms, rivers, or coastal surge
behaviourNotes: Move to higher ground. Stay put but grab your bag and be ready to evacuate the moment authorities advise it. [SG]
Don't walk through moving water higher than ankle height; if you must, use a stick to check the ground ahead of you. [SG]
In coastal or low-lying areas, a storm surge can flood the shoreline with little warning - move to high ground immediately. [HK]
Stock at least 3 days of food and water, and fill your bathtub in advance as a backup water supply. [KR]

name: Typhoon
tagline: Tropical storms with high winds & flooding
behaviourNotes: Keep a flashlight and first aid kit within reach - called out specifically for power outages and storm injuries. [SG]
Tune in to the radio for updates throughout the storm - don't step outside during a lull, winds can pick up again. [SG]
As the storm signal rises, finish preparations, stay indoors, lock windows and doors. [HK]
Lay in sandbags and waterproof flood gates, clear gutters, reinforce or bring in windows and loose outdoor objects. [TW]
